doc: Every game system the mashup touches. Rows with a null mechanism are not designed yet (they depend on what the real SM2 files turn out to contain).

rows.name: Start Dark Souls III through ModEngine2
rows.what: Play starts the game with the mashup's own ModEngine2 config, which loads the hook DLL.
rows.mechanism: modengine2_launcher.exe -t ds3 -p <DarkSoulsIII.exe> -c <generated toml> --modengine-dll <modengine2.dll>; the toml lists the hook DLL under external_dlls and the mod folder under mods

rows.name: Back up and verify the real save
rows.what: The player's real save is proven untouched after every session, or restored.
rows.mechanism: sha256 manifest of the real save folder before launch plus a full copy in {data}/backups; after the game exits compare, and restore from the copy if anything differs

rows.name: Private copy of the save
rows.what: The mashup plays its own copy of the player's character, created on first Play.
rows.mechanism: recursive copy (never move) of the real save folder to {data}/save on first Play; later Plays reuse the private copy

rows.name: Send save file access to the private copy
rows.what: Every file operation the game does under its real save folder lands in the private copy instead.
rows.mechanism: inline hooks (MinHook) on kernelbase file APIs rewrite any path under the real save folder to the private copy

rows.name: Keep the game offline
rows.what: The game process cannot reach any non-loopback network address.
rows.mechanism: inline hooks on ws2_32/winhttp/wininet entry points deny every non-loopback destination or host name; a WSAIoctl hook swaps ConnectEx for a guarded version

rows.name: Close the game if the sandbox is not in place
rows.what: If a sandbox hook cannot be installed the game does not run unprotected.
rows.mechanism: any hook installation error is logged and shown in a message box, then the process is terminated

rows.name: Diagnostic logs
rows.what: A plain log shows what the launcher and hooks did, so a failed test can be diagnosed.
rows.mechanism: append-only text files in {data}/logs with counts of redirected paths and denied connections

rows.name: Mark the game window
rows.what: The window title says this is the Ashen Marine offline copy, so screenshots and the player can tell.
rows.mechanism: SetWindowTextW on the game's top-level window once it exists, appending ' - Ashen Marine (offline copy)'

rows.name: Find the player's Space Marine 2
rows.what: The setup step locates the SM2 install itself, because Melty cannot see it.
rows.mechanism: read Steam's registry path, libraryfolders.vdf and appmanifest_2183900.acf to resolve steamapps/common/<installdir>

rows.name: Read SM2 files
rows.what: SM2's own weapon files are read from the player's install, never changed, never uploaded.
rows.mechanism: open each .pak read-only and read entries by name; never write, never launch or hook SM2

rows.name: Convert SM2 content for DS3
rows.what: SM2 sounds, textures, models and numbers become something Dark Souls III can use, in the mashup's private folder.
rows.mechanism: ashenmarine-setup prepare (read-only on the SM2 install): opens the client paks, reads sounds/desktop/wpn.bnk and wpn.zip, reads the bank objects exactly (hirc: sounds, random/switch/layer containers, volumes, delays; falls back to an approximate walk when the bank is not understood), plays each slot's Wwise event a few times in memory (seeded, reproducible), decodes the Wwise Vorbis media (ww2ogg algorithm, aoTuV 603 codebooks, lewton), mixes the layers into takes, brings all sounds up together to near full scale and writes {data}/assets/sounds/*.wav, index.json and ready.json; a report with the container trees goes to {data}/prepare-sm2; kit 0.5 reads the bank as version 150 really lays it out (the exact reading now covers the whole bank) and, when it does, writes a second set {data}/assets/sounds-exact next to the first (made as before, every sound at full volume); the hook switches between the two with F9 so the owner can compare

rows.name: Put the weapons in the player's inventory
rows.what: The chainsword and bolt pistol are in the inventory the first time the private save loads.

rows.name: Weapons look like SM2's
rows.what: The chainsword and bolt pistol show SM2's models and textures in Dark Souls III.
rows.mechanism: ashenmarine-setup (read-only on both games) reads the Dark Souls III weapon container (parts/wp_a_XXXX.partsbnd.dcx) from the archives and the Space Marine 2 template (tpl/wpn_*.tpl + .tpl_data) and its textures from the paks, and writes a copy of the DS3 container to {data}/mod/parts/ where ModEngine2 loads it instead of the archived one: the container keeps the DS3 weapon's skeleton, materials, dummy points and collision files; its model gets the SM2 full-detail geometry (the merged level-of-detail-0 sub mesh), re-encoded member by member in the DS3 model's own vertex layout and bound to the weapon's own bone (a container may hold more than one model: the Shortsword's has the weapon, WP_A_0200.flver, and its scabbard, WP_A_0200_1.flver, and the weapon is the model named like the texture file; the scabbard is shrunk to one tiny triangle because the Space Marine 2 chainsword has none, and left as it is if that cannot be done safely - kit 0.9 refused such containers outright); how the new model is placed comes from the weapons sheet where it says (`model_forward`/`model_up`: which way the weapon points and which way is up, `model_scale`, `model_hold_x/y/z`: where the hand holds it) and is worked out from the two shapes where it does not: matching the axes by length is right for the sword but would lay the Avelyn's replacement on its side (its bow limbs are as long as the crossbow) and make it as long as a rifle, so the bolt pistol is turned by the sheet, scaled like the chainsword (0.54) and held at the middle of its handle; its texture container gets the SM2 colour map re-encoded as a DS3 texture. Every step is checked (the model written again must be byte-identical to the game's file - kit 0.9 found that the writer put the wrong face count into the header of the real models, fixed in kit 0.10 and checked on all eight real weapon models - and the container written again must read back; sizes, counts and bounds must fit), and when anything is wrong nothing is written and an older file is removed. The first kits only report the structure of the DS3 files and (optionally) copy them so the converter can be written against real data; the look is a clearly labelled later upgrade of the same build

rows.name: Weapons sound like SM2's
rows.what: Swings, hits and shots play SM2's own sounds.
rows.mechanism: hook DLL, per-frame game task on the game's own thread: stamina and inventory counts through the darksouls3 crate (read-only), attack-button state through XInputGetState and GetAsyncKeyState (read-only), pure trigger state machines (ashen_common::triggers) decide when a slot fires, clips play through the private waveOut mixer; never touches the game's audio

rows.name: Read-only look at the running game (test kits)
rows.what: A private test kit reports facts about the player's own game (build, weapon table, inventory, stamina, text tables) so the weapons feature can be built on real data instead of guesses.
rows.mechanism: hook DLL thread: reads the exe's version resource and stops if the build is not one the darksouls3 crate knows; reads parameter tables, inventory and stats through the crate's typed structures from a per-frame game task; scans its own process memory with ReadProcessMemory for FMG text tables. Writes probe-ds3.* next to hook.log. Never writes game memory, never calls a game function.; kit 0.4 adds the row names of the weapon and goods tables, the references to item-name strings, and a time-based flush of the live-value samples; kit 0.9 adds a read-only look at ModEngine2's footprint in the program file (logs/me2-hook.txt: the bytes at the addresses ModEngine2's source hooks and patches, where a jump there leads by module name, and the counts of its loose-parameter signatures) to tell whether the loose files of the mod folder can be served at all in this build

rows.name: Report on Space Marine 2's weapon content
rows.what: The setup tool describes what the player's own SM2 install holds for a chainsword and a bolt pistol (files, textures, data, sounds), with preview pictures.
rows.mechanism: ashenmarine-setup probe: opens every client .pak read-only, lists weapon templates, decodes weapon textures to PNG previews, prints weapon .cls text, parses Wwise banks, recovers event names by hashing words from game text, reads wem headers; writes only to its own output folder

rows.name: Weapons are called what they are
rows.what: The test weapons show the names Chainsword, Bolt Pistol and Bolt Rounds in the inventory instead of the Dark Souls III names they are built from.
rows.mechanism: ashenmarine-setup ds3-prepare, read-only on the Dark Souls III install: opens the game's own archives (Data*.bhd/.bdt) with the public RSA keys found in the player's own exe or in {data}/cache/ds3-keys.pem, or - when no key is known - with the plain tables of contents that the test kit's collector saved from the running game into {data}/cache/bhd5 (the collector only READS the game's memory, checks everything against the player's own archives, and stops by itself); an archive whose .bhd is a plain BHD5 file (Data0) needs no key at all; finds the English item text by the hash of its path: msg/engUS/item_dlc2.msgbnd.dcx, item_dlc1.msgbnd.dcx and item.msgbnd.dcx, whichever of them the archives hold (the language folder of the English text is engUS; a fully updated game asks ModEngine2 for msg\engus\item_dlc2.msgbnd.dcx and never for item.msgbnd.dcx - kits 0.5 to 0.9 wrote only item.msgbnd.dcx, which is why the names never changed), and writes each changed copy under its own name (mod/msg/engus/<name>.msgbnd.dcx); when no archive has any of those hashes it looks at the first few KB of every file (DCX, then a BND4 whose files are .fmg text tables, then the text itself: Shortsword at id 2000000), so a different name or hash rule does not matter; reads it, changes only the weapon and ammunition name entries (and their descriptions) in a copy - each changed text table is changed in place: the new strings are put at the end of the table and the entries of the ids are pointed at them, so the layout the game's own tool chose (it is not the one this program would write: 0 of 47 tables came out byte-identical in kit 0.9) stays exactly as it is, and the old strings are wiped unless another entry still uses them - and writes that copy as a loose file into the ModEngine2 mod folder; every step is checked and nothing is written unless all checks pass (fail closed); the game's archives and files are never changed; the report also says how the game's own text tables differ from what this program writes (the first differing byte), because the game's loader is the final judge of the layout; kit 0.9: archives whose key is not known are told apart (every key the collector saw is tried on the first block of each archive and the plain start of any block that decrypts is shown), and the raw first and last bytes of every .bhd are in the report

rows.name: Weapons are called what they are, in the running game
rows.what: The test weapons show the names Chainsword, Bolter and Bolt Rounds in the inventory even when the item text of the archives cannot be read.
rows.mechanism: hook DLL thread (config features.rename, test kits): after the game has loaded its text it looks through the process's own committed private read-write memory with ReadProcessMemory for the exact UTF-16 strings of the base names (Shortsword, Avelyn, Standard Bolt: the whole string, a NUL right after it, no letter right before it) and overwrites each one in place with the live name from the weapons sheet (never longer than the old one, shorter ones padded with spaces, so a length stored next to the text stays true); the write uses WriteProcessMemory (an error instead of a fault); the pass repeats on a timer because the game builds its strings again when a world loads (kit 0.9 showed that this only reaches copies the game builds on the way: it wrote 741 strings and the inventory still showed the old names - the real cause was the file name of the loose item text, see item_names - so kit 0.10 does not start it); every address, the bytes around it and the result go to logs/rename.txt. It calls no game function and changes nothing else
